html:
The Nuwhaha were a Lushootseed speaking Coast Salish people of northwest Washington, in the Samish River valley and on the coast between Bay View and Bellingham.

They were known as a powerful and warlike people. Smallpox epidemics in the 1700s and 1800s devastated them, and wars with the Samish pushed them inland. In 1855 they signed the Treaty of Point Elliott. There is no separate Nuwhaha tribe today; their descendants belong to the Upper Skagit tribe, the Swinomish and the Samish.
sum: The Nuwhaha were a Lushootseed speaking Coast Salish people of northwest Washington, in the Samish River valley and on the coast between Bay View and Bellingham.
